body: Crackdown 2 is Ruffian Games' Xbox 360 open-world action game, first released in North America on 6 July 2010. The Agency's enhanced officers confront both the Cell organisation and infected creatures known as Freaks. As before, collecting orbs and performing activities improves the Agent's abilities, turning the city into a place whose possibilities expand with the character. Greater agility makes a roof easier to reach, while increased strength changes what can be used as a weapon. The sequel builds its appeal around that continuing transformation of movement and power.

Five skill areas connect progress to different actions. Shooting improves firearms, close combat builds strength and driving activities develop control of vehicles. Agility orbs provide an especially visible reason to explore high places, with later improvements allowing larger jumps and gliding. The player can therefore choose an activity partly for the capability it will strengthen. A street or rooftop is both a route through the city and an opportunity to develop the Agent. As those abilities grow, familiar places can be crossed more quickly or approached from a direction that was previously impractical.

The campaign supports up to four online cooperative players, expanding the original's shared play. Competitive modes allow larger groups to pursue different objectives, while the main world retains road and rooftop races as smaller tests of the Agent's abilities. Billy Thomson directed the project for Ruffian, with Kevin Riepl composing the music. Crackdown 3 followed in 2019. The second game continues the series' interest in making character development physically visible, so progress can be felt in the distance of a jump or the ease with which a once-difficult building is climbed.
